formats.key: PermitSingle(PermitDetails details,address spender,uint256 sigDeadline)PermitDetails(address token,uint160 amount,uint48 expiration,uint48 nonce)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature, Permit2 sets the signer's allowance so `spender` can pull up to `details.amount` of `details.token` from the signer through Permit2.
The allowance lasts until `details.expiration`. An expiration of 0 makes it valid only in the block where the permit is submitted.
An amount of type(uint160).max is never reduced on transferFrom, so it is an unlimited allowance.
The signer's stored nonce for (token, spender) goes up by one, and this replaces any earlier Permit2 allowance for that pair.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of token", with the spender as a raw address, the allowance amount in the token (or "Unlimited"), and the expiry date.

findings.title: PermitSingle shows the spender as a raw hex address, not as a named contract.
findings.evidence: descriptor PermitSingle field {"path":"spender","label":"Spender","format":"raw"}; case 0 shows Spender "0xE592427A0AEce92De3Edee1F18E0157C05861564" (Uniswap V3 SwapRouter), with no name.

findings.title: PermitSingle shows expiration 0 as a 1970 date, but Permit2 reads 0 as 'this block only'.
findings.evidence: Permit2 AllowanceTransfer/Allowance._updateApproval: `uint48 storedExpiration = expiration == BLOCK_TIMESTAMP_EXPIRATION ? uint48(block.timestamp) : expiration;` (BLOCK_TIMESTAMP_EXPIRATION = 0). Descriptor field details.expiration uses "format": "date" with no special case for 0.
findings.fix: Add a note or a threshold-style label for 0 (for example "Expires: current block only"), and add a test case with expiration 0.

findings.title: PermitSingle intent names no spender, token or amount, so the line alone does not say who gets what allowance.
findings.evidence: descriptor PermitSingle: "intent": "Authorize spending of token" and no interpolatedIntent.
findings.fix: Add "interpolatedIntent": "Allow {spender} to spend {details.amount}" after you make spender an addressName.

formats.key: PermitBatch(PermitDetails[] details,address spender,uint256 sigDeadline)PermitDetails(address token,uint160 amount,uint48 expiration,uint48 nonce)
effects: Once submitted, Permit2 sets one allowance per entry of `details`: `spender` can pull up to each `amount` of each `token` from the signer.
Each allowance has its own expiration. An expiration of 0 means the allowance is valid only in the submit block.
An amount of type(uint160).max is an unlimited allowance that is never reduced.
Each entry replaces the earlier Permit2 allowance for that (token, spender) pair and bumps its nonce.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens", with the spender as a raw address, then a list of all allowance amounts, then a separate list of all expiry dates.

findings.title: PermitBatch lists amounts and expiries as two separate arrays, so the signer cannot pair an expiry with its token.
findings.evidence: descriptor PermitBatch fields "details.[].amount" and "details.[].expiration" are separate fields. Case 1 and case 3 show "Amount allowance" twice, then "Approval expires" twice, with no token next to each expiry.
findings.fix: Show each entry as one group: {"path":"details.[]","fields":[{"path":"amount","label":"Amount allowance","format":"tokenAmount","params":{"tokenPath":"token",...}},{"path":"expiration","label":"Approval expires","format":"date","params":{"encoding":"timestamp"}}]}.

findings.title: PermitBatch shows the spender as a raw hex address, not as a named contract.
findings.evidence: descriptor PermitBatch field {"path":"spender","label":"Spender","format":"raw"}; case 1 shows Spender "0x68b3465833fb72A70ecDF485E0e4C7bD8665Fc45" (SwapRouter02) with no name.

findings.title: PermitBatch shows expiration 0 as a 1970 date, but Permit2 reads 0 as 'this block only'.
findings.evidence: Permit2 Allowance._updateApproval: `expiration == BLOCK_TIMESTAMP_EXPIRATION ? uint48(block.timestamp) : expiration`; descriptor details.[].expiration is a plain date.
findings.fix: Add a label or note for expiration 0, and a test case for it.

findings.title: PermitBatch intent names neither spender nor tokens.
findings.evidence: descriptor PermitBatch: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens", no interpolatedIntent.

formats.key: PermitTransferFrom(TokenPermissions permitted,address spender,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)
effects: One time, `spender` (who must be msg.sender) can move up to `permitted.amount` of `permitted.token` out of the signer's wallet before `deadline`.
The spender picks the recipient and the exact amount (requestedAmount <= permitted.amount) at submit time. The signed message holds neither.
The unordered nonce is spent, so the signature works once.
formats.shown: "Transfer {amount}" / "Authorize token transfer", with the spender by name, the amount ("Any amount" above 2^255) and the deadline.

findings.title: PermitTransferFrom reads as a fixed transfer, but the spender picks any amount up to the cap.
findings.evidence: Permit2 SignatureTransfer._permitTransferFrom: `if (requestedAmount > permit.permitted.amount) revert InvalidAmount(...)`; `ERC20(permit.permitted.token).safeTransferFrom(owner, transferDetails.to, requestedAmount)`. Descriptor: "interpolatedIntent": "Transfer {permitted.amount}", label "Amount". Case 4 renders "Transfer Any amount USDC".
findings.fix: Change the interpolatedIntent to "Allow {spender} to transfer up to {permitted.amount}" and the label to "Max amount".

findings.title: PermitTransferFrom recipient is not in the signed message, so no descriptor can show it.
findings.evidence: Permit2 SignatureTransfer.permitTransferFrom takes `SignatureTransferDetails calldata transferDetails` (to, requestedAmount) from the caller, outside the signed PermitTransferFrom struct; the format key has no recipient member.
findings.fix: Optionally say in the intent that the spender chooses the recipient.
